conventions.source: staging/blender/2026-11-20_elements/elements2.blend, scene Look, objects with el=elem2 (one station per element look, 40 m apart along x from 20000). Built by script from pass-2 element pieces and the new kit vfx_elements_kit_e2.fbx.
conventions.made: 2026-11-20 by Claude through the Blender MCP connection.
conventions.axes: Unity axes, metres. Unity x = -Blender x, Unity y = Blender z (up), Unity z = -Blender y. Assumes the kit FBX files are imported with Bake Axis Conversion so each kit object's local axes are Unity axes (as combos_recipe.json).
conventions.origin: Every position is relative to the main body's ground point (y = 0). Offsets are world-aligned to the combo camera (it looks along Unity +z from -z, 55 degrees down), not to the body's yaw. The player stands at player.position and faces the main body; "away from you" is the direction from the player to the main body.
conventions.groups: Pieces that share kit object and material are grouped. Each instance is [object, position, rotation_euler_deg, scale, placement], the KEY POSE (before any motion channel is applied). group.motion lists the same objects in the same order.
conventions.instance.rotation_euler_deg: Unity Euler angles in degrees (Quaternion.Euler(x, y, z)), rounded to 1 degree.
conventions.instance.position: Metres, rounded to 1 mm: the piece's pivot (its base centre, the kit convention).
conventions.instance.scale: A number for uniform scale, else [x, y, z] in Unity local axes.
conventions.instance.placement: g = on the ground, b = on or around a body.
conventions.group.kit_object: The object inside group.kit (pivot at the base centre). vfx_elements_kit_e2.fbx holds the meshes this pass needed that are in no earlier kit (see missing_from_kits), with their source rotation and scale baked in.
conventions.group.material: The material the piece wears in the render (shared meshes are re-coloured per piece).
conventions.timing: animated. Every piece is keyed in elements2.blend at 20 fps; time 0 is frame 7 (frames 1-6 are a 0.3 s lead-in).
conventions.motion: One entry per instance (same order): verb, note, visible [appear, vanish] s (a vanish of 9 means it stays), delay = appear time, duration = how long it shows within the GIF, easing (the easings its keys use), and the channels: path = [[t, offset (Unity axes, world-aligned), easing into this key]], scale_keys = [[t, multiplier on the key-pose scale (Unity local x, y, z), easing]], spin = {axis (Unity), keys [[t, degrees, easing]]} applied as Quaternion.AngleAxis(degrees, axis) * keyRotation about the pivot, orbit = {centre (Unity, from the main body), keys [[t, degrees, easing]]} applied last as Quaternion.AngleAxis(degrees, Vector3.up) about the centre, follow_body = the body index whose motion the piece rides on, redraw/strobe = the per-frame flicker. Before the first key a channel holds its first value, after the last its last. Easings: linear, out = 1-(1-x)^2, in = x^2, inout = smoothstep, outback = overshoot (c = 1.70158), step = jump at the key. Angles are already in Unity's sense (the sign is flipped from Blender's, which the god-move JSONs did not do for spin).
conventions.lead_in_and_settle: A piece whose window opens at 0 is already there in the lead-in; a piece whose window ends at the duration stays through the settle (0.5 s).
conventions.bodies: The enemy model (enemy_husk) per body, with its own motion (path, scale_keys, spin, visible); body 0 is the one the reaction lands on.
conventions.lights: None: every reaction is unlit beyond the scene sun.
